messages:
mira: quick sync — we've been toggling between REST and gRPC for the internal model-router/gateway path. i think this is biting us on headers and routing metadata.
alex: yup. main pain: we need reliable propagation of routing-decisions (tenant, model-variant, rollout-bucket) plus token accounting metadata for quota/telemetry. json bodies are easy but we lose type guarantees. grpc gives typing + smaller wire, but browser clients + some infra expect http/json.
sam: what if we split responsibilities: gRPC for internal service-to-service (router -> worker pool), and REST/JSON at the edge (api-gateway)? keep a clear contract at the gateway boundary.
priya: that makes sense operationally, but telemetry/quotas need consistent fields. we currently rely on headers like x-rw-tenant and x-rw-trace, but those headers get lost when we proxy/transcode or go through envoy.
mira: exactly. i've seen envoys drop unknown headers unless configured. and when we do http-json <-> grpc transcoding the payload encoding of the routing block becomes brittle.
alex: one approach: canonicalize routing metadata into a single header, e.g. x-rw-routing, base64-encoded protobuf. pros: typed payload, single header for proxies, smaller than JSON blob. cons: debugging is harder (opaque header) unless we add a decode helper.
sam: example? can you paste a proto sketch?
mira: sure — tiny example:

```proto
message RoutingMeta {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string model = 2;
  string variant = 3;
  string rollout_bucket = 4;
  int32 prompt_token_est = 5;
}
```

and we put grpc-serialized bytes into x-rw-routing (base64) when crossing HTTP proxies.
priya: i like typed routing meta. also lets us add fields later with backward compatibility. but we need clear rules: which services honor this header vs reading body.
alex: agree. implementation details:
- gateway: accept JSON from public clients, synthesize RoutingMeta and set x-rw-routing when proxying to internal services.
- internal router/workers: prefer gRPC APIs that take RoutingMeta as the canonical argument. fall back to header parsing for any http calls.
- envoy: configure to preserve x-rw-routing and not to log raw binary in access logs (privacy/size).
sam: quotas: should quota checks happen at gateway or at router? if gateway does quota enforcement we avoid double counting, but it's a choke point. if router does it, we need consistent token estimates propagated.
priya: idea: lightweight precheck at gateway using estimated tokens (prompt_token_est). gateway can reject obviously over-limit requests fast. final accounting happens at router/serve where exact token counts are observed and reported to billing/telemetry.
mira: rollout UX: for canaries we want to route subset of traffic to new variant. rollout decisions should be centralized in router to avoid gateway reloads. gateway should only carry the decision token (rollout_bucket) and not own the policy.
alex: for devex, add a small cli tool to decode x-rw-routing and print human-readable fields. also add a header-driven debug path: if x-rw-debug=true gateway dumps RoutingMeta into logs (redact tenant id when needed).
priya: telemetry notes: we need to emit model_choice, latency, tokens_in/tokens_out, and route_tags (canary/ab-test). ensure tracing spans correlate across gateway -> router -> worker using x-rw-trace or traceparent.
sam: ops concern: mixing grpc + net/http increases surface area for connection pools and deadlines. we should standardize timeouts: gateway->router 500ms for small ops, stream ops longer. document recommended keepalive and max concurrent streams.
mira: next steps / action items:
- alex: prototype header format + decode cli (deadline: EOD Fri)
- priya: propose envoy config snippets to preserve x-rw-routing and redaction rules (deadline: Tue)
- sam: draft RFC section on split responsibility (gateway precheck vs router authoritative) and timeout guidelines (deadline: next Wed)
- mira: add telemetry fields and mapping to our current metrics schema -> send to observability team for review (deadline: next Thu)
infra-bot: deploy:router-v2 started by @infra-cd at 2260001300 — rolling 3/12 hosts :spinner:
alex: noted infra-bot. i'll attach the prototype PR to the RFC thread once baseline is ready.
priya: also let's add a short runbook note: if x-rw-routing decode fails in router, default to safe-deny and emit alert to #eng-oncall.
sam: +1 — better to fail closed for routing metadata.
mira: thanks all — short sync tomorrow 10am to review prototypes. :thumbsup:
